cases.question: How accurate has this forecast actually been?
cases.answer: In the live track record, published forecasts scored an overall mean absolute error (MAE) of 6.31, beating CAMS on 52 of 54 days with a skill score of 41.3%. The rolling-origin backtest showed a mean skill vs CAMS of 43.3% across all lead times.

cases.question: Is this better than the Copernicus CAMS forecast?
cases.answer: Yes, this system beats the Copernicus CAMS forecast overall, with a skill vs CAMS score of 41.3% (beating CAMS in 52 of 54 days). Live track records show a lower mean absolute error (6.31) compared to CAMS's MAE of 10.741.

cases.question: How good is the 1-hour forecast?
cases.answer: The live track record for the 1-6 hour bucket shows a MAE of 4.808, with a skill vs CAMS of 0.557 and skill vs persistence of 0.241. cases.question: What drives the forecast the most?
cases.answer: The top driver behind the 24-hour forecast is measured minus CAMS (now) with a mean absolute SHAP value of 6.89. This is followed by the CAMS forecast for target hour (3.95) and forecast wind speed (3.3).

cases.question: Why does the model use CAMS as an input if CAMS is wrong?
cases.answer: Even though CAMS can be inaccurate on its own, the model uses it as a raw ingredient because its regional transport patterns still contain useful signals. By combining CAMS with local monitor data and other inputs, our model corrects those errors and outperforms CAMS, beating it in 52 of 54 days with a mean skill vs. CAMS of 0.433 in backtests (and an overall live MAE of 6.31 compared to CAMS's 10.741).
